The article mentions that a total of 450 patients were randomized, with 224 in the GDHT group and 226 in the control group. However, due to recruitment issues, they excluded orthopaedic patients, leaving 209 in GDHT and 211 in control. So, n_randomized_gdft is 209 and n_randomized_control is 211.

Next, the surgery types are specified. Most patients underwent major gastrointestinal surgery, with 150 in GDHT and 154 in control. Urological and gynaecological surgeries are also mentioned, but the exact numbers aren't provided for each group, so I'll note that the primary surgery was gastrointestinal.

For laparoscopy rates, the GDHT group had 105 laparoscopic procedures, and the control had 99. These numbers are provided in Table 2.

ASA physical status distribution is detailed in Table 1. GDHT has 14 (6.7%) ASA I, 134 (58.4%) ASA II, and 73 (34.9%) ASA III. Control has 35 (16.6%) ASA I, 116 (54.4%) ASA II, and 40 (19.0%) ASA III.

Looking at total fluids, both groups received similar amounts. GDHT had 1480 ml of crystalloid and 500 ml of colloid, while control had 1440 ml crystalloid and 500 ml colloid. Blood loss was around 200 ml in GDHT and 300 ml in control.

Inotrope use was 2 in GDHT and 1 in control, as per Table 2.

Morbidity events are clearly stated: 8.6% in GDHT and 16.6% in control. Mortality rates were both around 10%, so no significant difference.

Hospital LOS was 5 days in GDHT and 7 in control. Time to flatus, oral intake, and defecation are listed in Table 3, with GDHT showing earlier recovery in all these aspects.

Postoperative ileus isn't directly mentioned, so I'll mark that as NR.

I need to ensure all data points are correctly extracted and formatted as per the JSON structure, using the exact sections from the article where each piece of information was found.
